title: Exclusive labeling of direct and indirect pathway neurons in the mouse neostriatum
author: Okamoto, Yamauchi, et al.

steps.title: Inject AAV vector into mouse CPu
steps.instruction: Perform stereotaxic injection of the prepared AAV vector into the mouse caudate‑putamen (CPu) according to the referenced injection protocol.

steps.title: Perfuse and fix mouse brain
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse with 200 mg/kg sodium pentobarbital (Somnopentyl) IP, open the thoracic cavity, cut the right atrial appendage, insert a 22‑gauge needle into the left ventricle, perfuse 20 mL PBS for 3 min, then perfuse 20 mL fixative solution, remove the brain and postfix 12–24 h at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Filter PBS and fixative solution through filter paper before perfusion.
Avoid bubbles during perfusion to ensure complete fixation.

steps.title: Cryoprotect and freeze brain tissue
steps.instruction: Replace fixative with 30 % (w/v) sucrose in 0.1 M PB, gently shake 1–2 days at 4 °C; 30 min before sectioning set the low‑temperature circulator to 4 °C; mount brain in OCT on the freezing microtome stage, set electro‑freezing to –25 °C, quickly freeze with dry‑ice powder for ≥5 min.

steps.title: Section brain into 20‑µm slices
steps.instruction: Cut the frozen brain into 20‑µm‑thick parasagittal sections, collect sections with a paintbrush into six vials each containing 0.02 % (w/v) sodium azide in 0.1 M PB (≈20 sections per vial). For long‑term storage increase sodium azide to 0.2 %.

steps.title: Double immunofluorescence staining
steps.instruction: Perform double IF for GFP and RFP on free‑floating sections at 20–25 °C with gentle shaking.

substeps.instruction: Wash sections twice with 8 mL PBS for 10 min each, then with PBS‑X for 30 min.
Incubate 12–24 h in 500 µL PBS‑XCD containing 20 µg/mL chicken anti‑GFP and 1 µg/mL rabbit anti‑mRFP1.
Wash twice with 8 mL PBS‑X for 10 min each.
Incubate 2 h in 500 µL PBS‑XCD containing 5 µg/mL AlexaFluor 488 anti‑chicken IgY and 5 µg/mL AlexaFluor 568 anti‑rabbit IgG.
Wash PBS‑X 20 min twice, then PBS 20 min twice.
Mount sections on APS‑coated slides, apply coverslip with fluorescence mounting medium, store at –20 °C (≈2 years).
Observe with confocal laser scanning microscope.

steps.title: Prepare ABC peroxidase complex
steps.instruction: Mix solutions A and B of the ABC Elite kit each at 1:100 dilution in 500 µL PBS‑X, incubate ≥30 min at 20–25 °C with gentle shaking to form the avidin‑biotinylated peroxidase complex.

steps.title: Immunoperoxidase staining with BT‑GO amplification
steps.instruction: Carry out peroxidase‑based signal amplification on sections at 20–25 °C with gentle shaking.

substeps.instruction: Wash 8 mL PBS for 10 min twice.
Incubate 30 min in 8 mL 1 % (v/v) H₂O₂ in PBS to quench endogenous peroxidase.
Wash PBS‑X 10 min twice.
Incubate 12–24 h in 500 µL PBS‑XCD with 0.1 µg/mL rabbit anti‑GFP or anti‑mRFP1.
Wash PBS‑X 10 min twice.
Incubate 2 h in 500 µL PBS‑XCD with 10 µg/mL biotinylated goat anti‑rabbit IgG.
Wash PBS‑X 10 min twice.
Incubate 1 h in 500 µL PBS‑X with 1:100‑diluted ABC complex.
Wash PBS‑X 10 min twice, then 0.1 M PB 10 min twice.
Incubate 5 min with BT‑GO mixture (1:50 000‑diluted BT solution, 3 µg/mL glucose oxidase, 1 % BSA in 1 mL 0.1 M PB).
Add 10 µL β‑D‑glucose to reach 2 mg/mL, mix, then incubate 30 min.
Wash 0.1 M PB 10 min, then PBS‑X 10 min twice.
Incubate 1 h with 1:100‑diluted ABC in 500 µL PBS‑X.
Wash PBS‑X 10 min twice, then PBS 10 min twice.
Develop with 0.02 % (w/v) DAB and 0.0001 % (v/v) H₂O₂ in 8 mL 50 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 7.6) for 30–60 min, monitoring under microscope; add extra H₂O₂ if signal is weak.
Wash PBS 10 min three times.

steps.title: Dehydrate, clear, and mount sections
steps.instruction: Process stained sections for bright‑field imaging and long‑term storage.

substeps.instruction: Mount all sections serially on APS‑coated slides and dry.
Soak slides in 30 %, 50 %, and 70 % (v/v) ethanol‑water for 30 min each, then dip in 95 % ethanol.
Soak in 100 % ethanol for 12–24 h.
Soak in 50 % xylene‑ethanol then 100 % xylene for 12–24 h.
Coverslip with NEW MX mounting medium.
Observe under bright‑field microscope, capture images with Nikon D‑700.
Specimens can be stored ≥10 years at 20–25 °C protected from light.

description: We developed a method using an adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector system to label two groups of neurons with different fluorescent proteins. The vector contains a flip-excision (FLEX) switch (Schnutgen et al., 2003), and expresses GFP or RFP based on the expression, or the lack, of Cre recombinase (Figures 1A and 1B). This labeling method offers a great advantage for the simultaneous labeling of mutually exclusive systems in the nervous system, such as excitatory and inhibitory neurons.Figure 1Exclusive labeling of Cre-positive and -negative cells by an AAV vector(A) Construct of the AAV vector. The vector expresses RFP or GFP in the absence or presence of Cre recombinase by a flip-excision (FLEX) switch. Both GFP and RFP are tagged with a membrane-targeting protein, palmitoylation signal (pal).(B) Schematic diagram of the exclusive labeling method. Two cell populations are selectively labeled with different fluorescent proteins based on the expression of Cre recombinase.BGHpA, a polyadenylation signal derived from bovine growth hormone gene; E/SYN, enhanced human synapsin I promoter (Hioki et al., 2007); ITR, inverted terminal repeat. After preparation of the AAV vector, we injected the vector into the mouse neostriatum (caudate-putamen, CPu), and then analyzed the axonal projections of direct and indirect pathway medium-sized spiny neurons (dMSNs and iMSNs) (Okamoto et al., 2020). The production and purification methods of AAV vectors have been described in previous studies (Hamamoto et al., 2017; Ito et al., 2015; Iwano et al., 2018; Kataoka et al., 2014; Sohn et al., 2016; Sohn et al., 2017; Suzuki et al., 2015). We have also recently established a method to stably obtain a high-titer virus solution by recovering virus particles from cell pellets and the supernatant (medium) (Takahashi et al., 2020).
